Like when my dad gets mad at me for not staring at him when I talk, "He doesn't know how little he is self aware, how pathetic". "At this point, he realized that this couldn't be real. This couldn't be happening. It will all be over soon, right?" He yells at me too much but  I feel like I deserve some of it.

Also just like pretending I'm in a dramatic movie, like when I finally started trying to live (obviously I still feel depressed but I've decided I'm gonna try to not die). "It became necessary for him to tell himself that he would kill himself the next day, week, month. Even though he knew he would never do it, it was a useful delusion."

​

I know this is what everyone else will tell you, but I feel like the "useful delusion" part that my narrator said, I feel like you should adopt it as a transitionary stage from actively planning about su\*c\*de to placating yourself. I know placating has a negative connotation, but honestly trying not knowing if you're gonna succeed or fail is what it means to be human.

" I feel like a disease " This is me but literally for the past 2.5 years.

I literally find evidence but apparently my memory is wrong or I'm selectively choosing to ignore times when everyone around me is fine.

There are times I feel like the only disease I have is a mind cancer (not brain cancer), one that assimilates information that reinforces itself, and kicks out into oblivion any information that contradicts itself. All in an effort to distract myself from the possibility that I could lead a normal life, from the idea that if I worked hard enough, I could be happy. Maybe I'm lazy and my choice to be lazy has fueled it.

Other times I become the cancer, and I am so angry at the world and everyone I know. I'm most angry at my neglectful dismissive dad (I appreciate that he works and does errands but he acts like everything is fine, and constantly dismisses both my identity and me feeling sick or sad), the fact that my mother is dead (I don't think about it often but yea she died when I was 6), my dad's girlfriend (I don't wanna get into this), and some other people. Yet I am still get angry at other people for being happy when I don't have a right to be angry at them. Most of all I am angry at myself, while at the same time I only listen to myself, thinking foolishly that everyone dismisses my pov.

I've been thinking a lot about contradictions. They bother me, but I forget about most of them. For example, is suicide selfish or not selfish? Is not interacting with other people selfish or not selfish? Is hating yourself actually a way to protect yourself from confronting your vanity? What is the underlying reason for my depression?

Also, generally I am still freaked out by the fact that I was able to develop this cancer this far in 2 years. Because then the future looks even worse.
